title: A time average has no positive uniform information bound for onset inputs in symmetric passive circuit models
abstract: We tested how a time average preserves constant-input information when the input starts at recording onset in a symmetric passive stochastic circuit. The initial state was stationary before the input and independent of its amplitude. With full exact observation, known decay and unit independent current noise, we derived an exact eigenmode formula. The average-to-path Fisher information ratio tends to zero as the window shrinks. Keeping the initial population state changes the short-window limit to 75 percent. An endpoint difference and a weighted time integral retain all path information. Uniform scaling of a fixed electrical Laplacian cannot reduce average information, while path information stays equal to duration. In models from two partial adult worm maps, primary median average fractions were 0.008694 and 0.008696 at 0.01 leak times. Keeping the initial state raised both to about 0.751091. Independent covariance checks agreed within relative error 4.08e-15. The results extend a prior equilibrium-input bound to an input-onset case. They are model results, with no fitted activity data, measurement noise, or partial observation. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, figure and external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Median retained information over 180 point inputs per adult map. Solid curves use the population time average. The dashed curve also uses the initial population state. Unit leak, current noise and capacitance are model assumptions.
